commit.message:
mcp: skip non-message events in SSEClientTransport (#1439)

`SSEClientTransport` hands the data of every event that follows the
`endpoint` event to the connection, whatever the event's name. The
2024-11-05 transport sends server messages as SSE `message` events, and
an event without a name is a `message` event, so anything else carries
no JSON-RPC message: a keep-alive such as `event: ping` / `data: ping`,
or an event with no data, like a lone `id:` or `retry:` field.
`sseClientConn.Read` fails to decode it, and jsonrpc2 treats the read
error as the end of the connection: the session closes and calls in
flight fail with the `unmarshaling jsonrpc message: ...` decode error.

The streamable client already skips these events in `processStream`
(#636, #637), and the `sseClientConn` doc comment says reads are SSE
'message' events, but the goroutine in `SSEClientTransport.Connect` that
feeds `sseClientConn.incoming` never got the same check.

This change makes that goroutine skip events whose name is neither empty
nor `message`, and events without data, which is the same check
`processStream` makes. Message events are delivered as before. The
handling of the first event, which must be `endpoint`, is unchanged.

`TestSSEClientTransportSkipsNonMessageEvents` follows
`TestSSEClientTransportBufferedEvents`: it serves an `endpoint` event,
then a `ping` event with data, a `ping` event without data, an id-only
event, an unnamed message and a `message` event, and checks that `Read`
returns the two notifications in order. On current main the first `Read`
should get the `ping` data and return the decode error.

I have not compiled or run this: no Go toolchain was available where I
wrote it, so the expected failure on main comes from reading the code,
and I am relying on CI for the build and the test run. I did not file an
issue first, since the change is confined to the SSE client's event
loop.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
oauthex: encode and decode client metadata "jwks" as a JSON object (#1435)

Fixes #1422.

RFC 7591 §2 defines the `jwks` client metadata as a JSON object, but
`ClientRegistrationMetadata.JWKS` is a `string`. `RegisterClient`
therefore failed on any registration response that included `jwks` (Ory
Hydra returns `"jwks": {}` on every registration), and a JWK Set passed
by value was sent as a JSON string.

As suggested in the issue, the custom `MarshalJSON` and `UnmarshalJSON`
are on `ClientRegistrationMetadata`, so both the request and the
response are covered. `JWKS` keeps its type and now holds the JWK Set as
JSON text:

- Encoding: a value that is a JSON object is sent as an object. Any
other non-empty value is still sent as a JSON string, as before.
- Decoding: an object is stored as its JSON text, a JSON string is
stored as its contents (the previous behavior), and `null` leaves it
empty. Other JSON types are an error.

`ClientRegistrationResponse` embeds `ClientRegistrationMetadata`, so its
existing methods could no longer embed an alias of itself: the metadata
methods would be promoted through the alias and encode only the
metadata. They now use a struct that lists the response fields next to
the metadata.

Tests cover both types in both directions (`{}`, a key set, the string
form, `null`, a non-object, and the string fallback on encode), plus a
`RegisterClient` round trip with the response from the issue. The new
object cases fail on main. `go test ./...` and `go vet ./...` pass.

Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commit.message:
conformance: run the client credentials scenario (#1433)

`conformance/baseline.yml` listed `auth/client-credentials-basic` among
the "OAuth mechanisms not implemented by the Go MCP SDK", but
`extauth.ClientCredentialsHandler` has implemented the client
credentials grant with a client secret since #895. The conformance
client had no handler for the scenario, so the suite never exercised it:

```
Unknown scenario: "auth/client-credentials-basic"
[client-credentials-basic-auth] FAILURE Client did not make a client_credentials token request
```

This registers a scenario handler that authorizes with
`ClientCredentialsHandler`, using the client ID and secret the scenario
provides, and removes the scenario from the baseline.
`auth/client-credentials-jwt` stays in the baseline:
`ClientCredentialsHandler` only supports client secrets.

With conformance 0.2.0-alpha.11 (the version CI uses),
`auth/client-credentials-basic` passes 9/9 checks, and the full client
suite run with the baseline reports "Baseline check passed: all failures
are expected."

`go test ./...`, `go test -race` on `auth` and `mcp`, `go vet ./...` and
staticcheck v0.6.1 pass.

Co-authored-by: Guglielmo Colombo <guglielmoc@google.com>

commit.message:
auth/extauth: fix token source lifetime and concurrent access in the handlers (#1432)

Fixes #1430.
Fixes #1431.

Two fixes to how the `extauth` handlers manage their token source. They
change the same lines of `ClientCredentialsHandler.Authorize`, so they
come in one PR, one commit each.

**Token source bound to the `Authorize` context (#1430)**

`ClientCredentialsHandler.Authorize` built its token source with
`clientcredentials.Config.TokenSource(ctx)`, where `ctx` is the context
passed to `Authorize`. `clientcredentials` keeps that context and uses
it for every later token request. The transport calls `Authorize` from a
request- or connect-scoped context and keeps using the token source for
the whole connection, so once that context was done and the first access
token expired, every request failed with `context canceled`.
`setMCPHeaders` only re-authorizes after an `invalid_grant`
`RetrieveError`, so the connection did not recover. #988 fixed the same
problem in `AuthorizationCodeHandler`.

The first token is now requested with `ctx`, so that `Authorize` still
honors its context, and the token source used afterwards is built on a
background context that carries the configured HTTP client. The fake
authorization server now applies `Config.AccessTokenTTL` to the
client_credentials grant too, so tests can make its token expire.

**Unsynchronized token source (#1431)**

`ClientCredentialsHandler` and `EnterpriseHandler` wrote their
`tokenSource` (and, for `ClientCredentialsHandler`, `grantedScopes`) in
`Authorize` and read it in `TokenSource` without synchronization. The
streamable client transport calls `Authorize` for any request that fails
with 401 or 403, and `TokenSource` before every request, so concurrent
requests race on that state. `AuthorizationCodeHandler` guards the same
fields with a mutex since #1058. Both handlers now guard them with a
`sync.RWMutex`.

**Tests**

- `TestClientCredentialsHandler_TokenAfterContextCancel`: after the
context passed to `Authorize` is cancelled, the token source still gets
a new token once the first one has expired. Fails without the first
commit.
- `TestClientCredentialsHandler_ConcurrentAuthorize` and
`TestEnterpriseHandler_ConcurrentAuthorize`: run `Authorize` and
`TokenSource` from several goroutines. Fail under the race detector
without the second commit.

`go test ./...`, `go test -race` on `auth` and `mcp`, `go vet ./...`,
staticcheck v0.6.1 and the client conformance suite (0.2.0-alpha.11, run
as in CI with the baseline) pass.

---------

Co-authored-by: Guglielmo Colombo <guglielmoc@google.com>

commit.message:
mcp: marshal ResourceNotFoundError data as JSON (#1427)

`ResourceNotFoundError` built its data with `fmt.Sprintf` and `%q`. Go's
quoting is not JSON: it escapes DEL as `\x7f` and some non-printable
runes (such as the tag characters in flag emoji) as `\U000e0067`,
producing invalid JSON. Encoding the error response then fails, jsonrpc2
treats that as a broken writer and closes the connection, so a client
reading an unregistered resource with such a URI terminates the whole
session.

This change builds the data with `json.Marshal` instead. No exported API
changes.

Tests:
- `TestResourceNotFoundErrorData`: the data is valid JSON and
round-trips URIs containing DEL and a flag emoji.
- `TestReadUnregisteredResourceKeepsSession`: over in-memory transports,
`resources/read` of such an unregistered URI returns the not-found
error, and a subsequent `resources/list` on the same session still
succeeds.

Fixes #1426

AI assistance was used to prepare this change; I reviewed and tested it.

Co-authored-by: Guglielmo Colombo <guglielmoc@google.com>

commit.message:
mcp: send no response for a cancelled request on 2026-07-28 stdio sessions (#1267)

The cancellation utility of 2026-07-28 says that a server receiving
`notifications/cancelled` SHOULD "Not send a response for the cancelled
request". On that revision stdio is the transport that carries the
notification: over streamable HTTP, closing the response stream is the
cancellation and no notification is expected (see
`StreamableHTTPOptions.PropagateRequestCancellation`). This SDK answered
the cancelled request anyway, because `processResult` in
`internal/jsonrpc2/conn.go` writes the response with `notDone{req.ctx}`
and no application code runs in between.

This change drops that response on the stdio-style transports
(`StdioTransport`, `CommandTransport`, `IOTransport` and
`InMemoryTransport`) for sessions on 2026-07-28 or later. Sessions on
earlier versions, the SSE transport and the streamable transport keep
answering a cancelled request, which is why this updates #1259 rather
than fixing it.

- `internal/jsonrpc2`: `Connection.CancelFromPeer` is `CancelCause` for
a cancellation the peer asked for. Before it cancels the call's context,
it tells a writer that implements the new optional `ResponseDropper`
interface which call's response to drop. It does so under the
connection's lock, in the critical section that finds the request, and
`processResult` removes the request under the same lock before it writes
the response, so the writer is told either before it is handed the
response or not at all; `ResponseDropper` documents that `DropResponse`
runs with the lock held. The connection still writes the response once
the handler returns, and dropping it is the writer's decision. `Cancel`
and `CancelCause` keep their meaning, so the listens
`ServerSession.Close` cancels still get their results. A
`subscriptions/listen` that the client cancels with
`notifications/cancelled` is treated like any other cancelled request:
on these sessions it no longer gets its `SubscriptionsListenResult`.
- `mcp`: `canceller.Preempt` calls `CancelFromPeer` where #1390 calls
`CancelCause`, directly rather than in a goroutine. `ioConn` implements
`DropResponse` and discards the response to a dropped call when the
negotiated version is 2026-07-28 or later. `loggingConn` forwards
`DropResponse` and `sessionUpdated` to its delegate. The jsonrpc2
connection asks its writer for `ResponseDropper`, and `ServerSession`
asks its connection for `sessionUpdated`, which is how `ioConn` learns
the version `DropResponse` checks. Without the forwarders, a
`LoggingTransport` would hide both from `ioConn`. That also gives a
server-side `LoggingTransport` the session updates #1328 reports
missing; the client side of #1328 is not covered.
- `docs/protocol.md` says which transports and versions send no
response.

Tests: `TestCancelFromPeer` in `internal/jsonrpc2`, for a cancellation
from the peer and a local `Cancel`; `TestIOConnDropResponse`,
`TestIOConnCancelledCallGetsNoResponse` (end to end over an in-memory
transport wrapped in `LoggingTransport`) and
`TestLoggingConnDropResponse` in `mcp`.

Updates #1259.

---------

Co-authored-by: Guglielmo Colombo <guglielmoc@google.com>

commit.message:
mcp: detach SSE client event stream from the Connect context (#1403)

Fixes #1331

SSEClientTransport.Connect used the context passed to it for the
long-lived event stream. If the caller bounded the handshake with a
timeout or cancelled it afterwards, the stream closed and later calls
failed. StreamableClientTransport does not behave this way.

This change makes the stream independent of the Connect context. The
context now only bounds the handshake: if it is cancelled before the
handshake completes, Connect returns the error and cleans up the
request. After Connect returns, the stream is cancelled only by Close.

Testing: added `TestSSEClientConnectContextCanceled` in
`mcp/sse_test.go`. It cancels the Connect context after connecting and
checks that a later Ping succeeds. The test and the project's checks
pass.

I use the usual pattern of a timeout context for Connect, and it broke
the SSE session without any warning. The streamable transport works with
the same code, so I wanted both to behave the same.

Co-authored-by: Guglielmo Colombo <guglielmoc@google.com>

mcp: detach SSE client event stream from the Connect context (#1403)

Fixes #1331

SSEClientTransport.Connect used the context passed to it for the
long-lived event stream. If the caller bounded the handshake with a
timeout or cancelled it afterwards, the stream closed and later calls
failed. StreamableClientTransport does not behave this way.

This change makes the stream independent of the Connect context. The
context now only bounds the handshake: if it is cancelled before the
handshake completes, Connect returns the error and cleans up the
request. After Connect returns, the stream is cancelled only by Close.

Testing: added `TestSSEClientConnectContextCanceled` in
`mcp/sse_test.go`. It cancels the Connect context after connecting and
checks that a later Ping succeeds. The test and the project's checks
pass.

I use the usual pattern of a timeout context for Connect, and it broke
the SSE session without any warning. The streamable transport works with
the same code, so I wanted both to behave the same.
